criteria.text: The participant has histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC with Stage IIIB-IIIC or Stage IV disease, not suitable for curative intent radical surgery or radiation therapy.
For Part B and Safety Lead-In Part B, the histology of the tumor must be predominantly non-squamous (in line with pemetrexed label).
The participant has disease with evidence of KRAS G12C mutation.
The participant has known programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression.
For Part A, the PD-L1 expression is greater than or equal to (≥)50 percent (%).
For Part B, the PD-L1 expression is 0% to 100%.
For Part C, the PD-L1 expression is <50%.
The participant has measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.
The participant has an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
The participant has an estimated life expectancy ≥12 weeks.
The participant has the ability to swallow capsules.
The participant has adequate laboratory parameters.
The participant's contraceptive use is consistent with local regulations for those participating in clinical studies.
Women of childbearing potential must meet the following requirements.
The participant has a negative pregnancy test.
The participant is not breastfeeding during treatment.

The participant has a documented additional validated targetable oncogenic driver mutation or alteration in genes such as epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), BRAF (V600E), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), MET (exon 14), ROS1, rearranged during transfection (RET), or neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK)1/2/3.
The participant has had any of the following prior to randomization.
The participant has had prior systemic therapy (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, or biological therapy) for advanced or metastatic NSCLC.
The participant has had 1 cycle of standard-of-care treatment prior to study enrollment for cases where immediate treatment is clinically indicated.
The participant has known active central nervous system metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.
The participant has predominantly squamous cell histology for NSCLC.

For participants with mild to moderate renal insufficiency, the participant is unable to avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) two days before (5 days for long acting NSAIDs), day of, and two days after administration of pemetrexed.
The participant is unable or unwilling to take folic acid or vitamin B12 supplementation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study of First-Line Olomorasib (LY3537982) and Pembrolizumab With or Without Chemotherapy in Patients With Advanced KRAS G12C-Mutant Non-small Cell Lung Cancer". Your earlier answers already covered 6 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told that your lung cancer is Stage IIIB, IIIC, or Stage IV, and that surgery or radiation to cure it is not an option?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, but I don't think so. They said they caught it early and that surgery can take it out, so I don't believe it's advanced like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. To be sure, has a doctor ever told you that your cancer is Stage IIIB, IIIC, or Stage IV, or that surgery/radiation to cure it is not an option?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, but no. They said it's just one spot and surgery can take it out, so I don't think it's that advanced.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your lung cancer is non-squamous? This is a specific type of lung cancer. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't remember the type. I'm not sure if it's squamous or non-squamous.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your cancer has a KRAS G12C mutation? This is a specific genetic change in the tumor. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I think they tested for something like that but I don't know the result.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your cancer has been tested for PD-L1 expression? This is a test that looks at a specific protein on the cancer cells. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I'm not sure if they did that test or what the result was.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your PD-L1 test result was 50% or higher? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I'm not sure what the result was.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your current health, do you expect to live for at least 12 weeks? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I'm doing everything I always did, work and all, but I'm not sure how long I'll live.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to swallow capsules? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, yes, I can swallow capsules just fine. I take my vitamins every day without any trouble.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any blood tests or lab work done in the last 7 days to check your blood counts and organ function?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I'm not sure when my last blood work was done.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently use any form of birth control or contraception? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I'm not, sorry. I'm 55 and not pregnant or breastfeeding.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any prior treatment for your lung cancer, such as chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any treatment yet. I'm sorry, I haven't had chemo or anything else.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you haven't had treatment yet, does your doctor feel that starting treatment immediately is clinically necessary for your lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I'm not sure if it's clinically necessary to start right now or if we can wait.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you're not sure, would you like me to ask your doctor if starting treatment right now is medically necessary for your lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, please do. I'm sorry, I really don't know what's best medically, so I'd appreciate it if you could ask my doctor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The trial asks about this: “For participants with mild to moderate renal insufficiency, the participant is unable to avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) two days before (5 days for long acting NSAIDs), day of, and two days after administration of pemetrexed.”. Does this describe you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I'm not sure if I have any kidney issues or if I need to avoid those pain medicines.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking folic acid or vitamin B12 supplements, or are you unable or unwilling to take them?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't know. I'm not sure if I take folic acid or B12 supplements.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
